title: Connectivity Troubleshooting
summary: Follow a layered, low-risk process for a synthetic network fault.
objectives: Check physical, interface, addressing, path, and name-resolution evidence in order.
Document a safe next step and escalation boundary.

vocab.def: The system area where evidence suggests a problem may be located.
Whether one system can successfully reach another in a defined test.
Passing responsibility or a problem to an authorized person or team.

sections.heading: Use layers
sections.body: Confirm the symptom, check link state, inspect the interface, review address and gateway evidence, trace the path, then check DNS when relevant. Each step narrows possibilities without random changes.

sections.heading: Stop at the boundary
sections.body: If the next action involves live fiber, an unauthorized target, or a change outside the sandbox, stop, document, and escalate. Safe troubleshooting includes knowing when not to act.

practice.prompt: A device has an IP address, can reach its gateway, and cannot resolve a service name. Which fault domain is most relevant first?
practice.answer: Name resolution or DNS is the most relevant first fault domain in this synthetic scenario.

quiz.question: What should happen before changing a network configuration?
options: Confirm the symptom and gather evidence
quiz.answer: Confirm the symptom and gather evidence

criteria: Uses relevant topology and connectivity evidence
Recommends a safe next action and escalation

lab.objective: Diagnose and document a synthetic connectivity fault.

reflectionPrompt: Which troubleshooting step reduced uncertainty most, and what remained unknown?
